The test image shows an opened soybean pod with:
- White, cottony/fluffy material coating the inside of the pod walls
- Brown discoloration on the pod interior
- Green seeds that appear relatively normal
- The white fungal-looking growth filling the pod cavity

This strongly suggests White Mold (Sclerotinia), which is known for white cottony mycelium inside pods. Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference White Mold image shows bleached/collapsed stems and pods consistent with Sclerotinia infection. The test image's white cottony mycelium filling the pod interior is the hallmark sign of White Mold — the fungus grows inside pods producing fluffy white mycelium before forming sclerotia.
